items.prompt: A photorealistic photograph of a real full-size Hanseatic holk of about 1460, the big northern cargo ship of the Baltic and the North Sea: about 26 metres long, a very broad, deep, round-bellied hull with clinker-built overlapping planks, a strongly curved banana-shaped sheer rising high at both ends, a plain square sterncastle and a small forecastle built onto the hull. ONE single tall mast amidships carrying ONE very large square sail of undyed linen, no topsail, a round fighting top at the masthead, and a small lateen mizzen near the stern. A plain working ship: no carving, no gilding, no windows, no flags, no gunports, no decoration. Important: the bowsprit at the bow (right) carries no sail at all, no triangular jib and no staysail; the only triangular sail is the small lateen on the mizzen mast at the stern (left end). Seen exactly side-on, bow pointing right, warm late afternoon light from the right, the same light and style as the reference photo. Weathered sails, hemp rigging, dark tarred planking. Not a fantasy ship, not a pirate ship, not a model: a real ship, photographed. She is isolated on a solid, flat, evenly lit chroma-key green background (#00b140) filling everything around her, including below the hull: no sea, no sky, no shadow, no floor, no stand, no cradle. The whole ship from the mastheads to the keel in frame, with a margin all round.
